html_lesson_6:slide:0.title: The Box Model 📦
html_lesson_6:slide:0.content:
Every HTML element is a box! The box model consists of:

• Content - The actual text/image
• Padding - Space around content
• Border - Line around padding
• Margin - Space outside border

html_lesson_6:slide:1.title: Padding
html_lesson_6:slide:1.content: Padding creates space inside the element, between content and border.

html_lesson_6:slide:2.title: Margin
html_lesson_6:slide:2.content: Margin creates space outside the element, separating it from other elements.

html_lesson_6:slide:3.title: Border
html_lesson_6:slide:3.content: Borders wrap around padding and content.

html_lesson_6:question:0.explanation: Padding creates space inside the element, between content and border.

html_lesson_6:question:1.prompt: How do you center an element horizontally with margin?
html_lesson_6:question:1.explanation: margin: 0 auto; sets top/bottom to 0 and left/right to auto, centering the element.

html_lesson_6:question:2.prompt: What is the default box-sizing value?
html_lesson_6:question:2.explanation: By default, box-sizing is content-box, where width/height only apply to content. border-box includes padding and border in the dimensions.

html_lesson_6:question:3.prompt: What happens when you set box-sizing: border-box?
html_lesson_6:question:3.explanation: border-box makes width/height include padding and border, making sizing more predictable.

options.html_lesson_6:question:3:option:1: Padding and border are included in the element's width/height

html_lesson_6:question:4.explanation: Margin collapse occurs when vertical margins of adjacent elements overlap, and the larger margin wins.

options.html_lesson_6:question:4:option:1: When vertical margins between elements combine into one

html_lesson_8.title: CSS Grid Basics
html_lesson_8.description: Build two-dimensional layouts with CSS Grid

html_lesson_8:slide:0.title: What is CSS Grid? 📐
html_lesson_8:slide:0.content:
CSS Grid is perfect for 2D layouts with rows AND columns.

Use cases:
• Page layouts
• Image galleries
• Card grids
• Dashboard layouts

html_lesson_8:slide:1.title: Grid Container
html_lesson_8:slide:1.content: Enable grid and define columns and rows.

html_lesson_8:slide:2.title: Grid Units
html_lesson_8:slide:2.content: Different ways to size grid tracks.

html_lesson_8:slide:3.title: Placing Items
html_lesson_8:slide:3.content: Control where items appear in the grid.

html_lesson_8:question:0.prompt: What does "1fr" mean in CSS Grid?
html_lesson_8:question:0.explanation: fr is a fractional unit that divides available space proportionally.

html_lesson_8:question:1.prompt: How do you create 4 equal columns?

html_lesson_9.title: Responsive Design
html_lesson_9.description: Make your websites work on all screen sizes

html_lesson_9:slide:0.title: Why Responsive? 📱
html_lesson_9:slide:0.content:
Users browse on many devices:

• Desktop computers (1920px+)
• Laptops (1024-1920px)
• Tablets (768-1024px)
• Phones (320-768px)

Your design must adapt to all of them!

html_lesson_9:slide:1.title: Viewport Meta Tag
html_lesson_9:slide:1.content: Essential for mobile browsers to render correctly.

html_lesson_9:slide:2.title: Media Queries
html_lesson_9:slide:2.content: Apply different styles based on screen size.

html_lesson_9:slide:3.title: Mobile-First Approach
html_lesson_9:slide:3.content: Start with mobile styles, then add complexity for larger screens.

html_lesson_9:question:0.prompt: What does the viewport meta tag do?
html_lesson_9:question:0.explanation: The viewport meta tag tells mobile browsers how to render the page width.

html_lesson_9:question:1.explanation: Mobile-first means writing base styles for mobile, then using media queries to enhance for larger screens.

options.html_lesson_9:question:1:option:2: Start with mobile, add for larger screens

html_lesson_9:question:2.prompt: What does min-width in a media query mean?
html_lesson_9:question:2.explanation: @media (min-width: 768px) means "apply these styles when the viewport is 768px or wider".

options.html_lesson_9:question:2:option:1: Applies styles when screen is AT LEAST this wide

html_lesson_9:question:3.explanation: Common breakpoints target mobile (~480px), tablet (~768px), and desktop (~1024px+) devices.

html_lesson_9:question:4.prompt: Why use relative units (%, em, rem) instead of pixels for responsive design?
html_lesson_9:question:4.explanation: Relative units scale proportionally and respect user accessibility settings, making designs more flexible and accessible.

options.html_lesson_9:question:4:option:1: They adapt better to different screen sizes and user preferences

html_lesson_10.title: CSS Transitions & Animations
html_lesson_10.description: Add motion and interactivity to your designs

html_lesson_10:slide:0.title: CSS Transitions ✨
html_lesson_10:slide:0.content:
Transitions smoothly animate changes between two states.

Use for:
• Hover effects
• Focus states
• Color changes
• Size changes

html_lesson_10:slide:2.title: CSS Animations
html_lesson_10:slide:2.content: For more complex, multi-step animations, use @keyframes.

html_lesson_10:question:0.prompt: What is the difference between transition and animation?
html_lesson_10:question:0.explanation: Transitions animate between two states, while animations use @keyframes for complex multi-step sequences.

options.html_lesson_10:question:0:option:1: Transition needs 2 states, animation uses keyframes

html_lesson_10:question:1.explanation: infinite makes the animation repeat indefinitely.

html_lesson_10:question:2.prompt: What is the purpose of animation-timing-function?
html_lesson_10:question:2.explanation: animation-timing-function (ease, linear, ease-in, ease-out, etc.) controls how the animation progresses over time.

options.html_lesson_10:question:2:option:1: Controls the speed curve of the animation

html_lesson_10:question:3.prompt: When should you use transitions vs animations?
html_lesson_10:question:3.explanation: Use transitions for simple state changes (hover effects). Use @keyframes animations for multi-step, complex motion.

options.html_lesson_10:question:3:option:1: Transitions for simple 2-state changes, animations for complex sequences

html_lesson_10:question:4.explanation: forwards makes the element retain the styles from the last keyframe after the animation completes.

options.html_lesson_10:question:4:option:1: Keeps the final animation state after completion
